analysis: Exponential recency weighting (0.9 per position) achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.5175, below the previously reported 0.5200 by 0.0025, while remaining above the reported 0.505 baseline. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.560, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.595, Electronics 0.395, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.520. Electronics declined from the reported 0.400 to 0.395. This trial does not support the hypothesized improvement from emphasizing recent transitions; the small aggregate difference does not establish causality. The host completed training and evaluation successfully.
code_summary: One independent RecurrentMemory model per category combines item embeddings, a GRU, jointly trained causal attention, gated memory, residual layer normalization, dropout, and learned item bias. Training uses 32 sampled negatives with context/positive masking, sampled-softmax ranking loss plus 0.2 times auxiliary positive and negative BCE losses. All losses use normalized exponential recency weights; negative BCE first averages allowed negatives within each position. AdamW, scheduling, clipping, sampling, seeds, and checkpoint selection remain unchanged. Dataset routing loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category; the predictor writer exports the matching architecture. No ensemble or separate scoring component is used.
